This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 18-03-2022 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the bicycle to reach his work location at logistics company namely M/s Transeasy Relocations India Pvt. Ltd.,
located at 32/1, 1st Floor, Chummy's Chalet, Garudachar Palya, Mahadevapura,
Bengaluru, by abiding the traffic rules.

When he was crossing the road infront of the said company, the rider of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EW-6038 came with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle of the petitioner from his left side.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to MTB Orthopaedic and Trauma Hospital, Mahadevapura,
Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working in Logistic Company and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Krishnarajapuram Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said scooter for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has admitted that, he is the registered owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and he is having valid driving licence and the vehicle is insured.
Further, he has contended that, he has not committed the alleged accident, he was not at all present in the alleged spot of accident, nor his vehicle was subject to any alleged accident.
Further, he has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the reason for not lifting the weight and heavy goods is due to the old age of the petitioner and not for the alleged accident.
He himself stated in the petition that, he was working in a logistic company, which itself create a doubt that the alleged injuries might have caused while he was lifting the heavy materials.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner has not approached this Hon'ble Tribunal with clean hands, the alleged accident was occurred on 18-03-2022, but the complaint was lodged on 10-05-2022.
So there is huge delay in filing the complaint to the nearby Police Sstation.

The delay of 52 days cannot be condoned, as there is a huge malafide intentions,
colluding with the police officers and other persons, who are inimical towards the respondent and there is a serious bad intentions behind the complaint.

If at all the alleged accident would have taken place why the petitioner has kept quiet for such a long period i.e. 52 days, there are no reasons assigned in the claim petition about the delay in filing the police complaint.
This claim petition is filed only to take undue advantage and the sole motive of the petitioner is to extract money from the respondent by one way or other.

Further it is contended that, the petition is liable to be dismissed Sudharsan Bengali vs Girish.S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66531843/
2 for non-joinder of necessary parties and there is no cause of action arose to file the present petition.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 18-03-2022 at about 9.30 a.m.,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Scooter, bearing registration No. KA-53-EW-6038 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

sentences.text: In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.2 is certified copy of order-sheet in AIR Misc. No.499/2022, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of accident intimation notice, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.7 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is certified copy of 'B' Register extract, Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 20), Ex.P.12 are salary certificates (total 3), Ex.P.13 is certificate, Ex.P.14 is certified copy of order sheet in CC No.33405/2022 and Ex.P.15 is computer generated copy of disability certificate.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.2 to 8, 14 and 15,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and dashing the same to the bicycle of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his right hand.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-EW-6038 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. On the other hand, the respondent has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, he has not caused the alleged accident, he was not at all present at the alleged place of accident, nor his vehicle was involved in the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police has falsely implicated the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 in the alleged accident.
But, the respondent has failed to establish the said contentions.
Except the self serving statement of the respondent/R.W.1, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent to establish the above contentions.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW- 6038 and dashing the same to the bicycle of the petitioner from his left side and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his hand in the said accident.
The evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Though the learned counsel for respondent cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
13. Further, as per the Motor Vehicles Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence Sudharsan Bengali vs Girish.S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66531843/
4 on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter.

sentences.text: There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to his sole negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of the accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

The investigation officer has also clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and dashing the same to the bicycle of the petitioner.
Admittedly the said charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-EW-6038.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending scooter in the accident,
rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 52 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner in his Ex.P.5 first information statement has clearly stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.

He has stated that, as he was taking treatment in the hospital and as he was living alone without any support of family member, he could not decide how to proceed legally and hence there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."

15. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.6 First Information Report and Ex.P.5 first information statement.

Further it is pertinent to note that, in the Ex.P.7 wound certificate it is clearly mentioned that, the petitioner was brought to MTB Orthopaedic and Trauma Hospital,
Bengaluru, on the date of accident itself, with an history of road traffic accident, taken place on 18-03-2022 at around 08:30 p.m., near TranseasyRelocation Services Pvt. Ltd. Company,
Garudacharpalya, Mahadevapura, Bengaluru.

Further, it was the duty of the concerned officer of the jurisdictional police to immediately visit the said hospital and record the statement of the victim.
There is no document forthcoming in the present case, with respect to discharge of their duty by the hospital authorities or the concerned officer of the jurisdictional Police Station.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the Ex.P.9 Discharge Summary clearly speaks that, the petitioner was referred to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru by M.T.B.
Hospital on the same day and the petitioner got admitted in the said hospital with an history of road Sudharsan Bengali vs Girish.S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66531843/
5 traffic accident, while he was riding a cycle was hit by a two wheeler on 18-03-2022 at 9-30 AM,
near Gowdachapalya, Mahadevepura and sustained injury to his right forearm.

In such circumstances the contention of the respondent that, no such accident as alleged by the petitioner has taken place at the given date, time and place of accident and the petitioner in collusion with the Police has falsely implicated the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 in the said accident and has got created false documents in order to claim compensation, does not hold good and are not sustainable.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate and Ex.P.9 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
As per the said documents, the petitioner has sustained right distal both bone forearm fracture.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that,
the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained right distal both bone forearm fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:

The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident he was working in Logistic Company and was earning sum of Rs.40,000/-
per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
To substantiate the same, he has produced computer generated copy of disability certificate, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
But, he has neither examined the author of said document, nor he has produced the original disability certificate.

Further, no where in the said certificate it is stated that,
the injuries mentioned in it have been caused to the petitioner in the accident in question.

Further,
he has not examined any doctor to establish that, he has suffered any disability or deformity due to injuries sustained in the said accident.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 20 medical bills and certificate, as per Ex.P.11 and 13.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the petitioner has not examined the author of Ex.P.13.

Further,
P.W.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that, there is no mention of mode of payment in Ex.P.13, he has paid the amount through cash, he has not produced any document to show the payment of amount to the physiotherapist, he has not produced any prescriptions given by the physiotherapist and he has made part payment to the physiotherapist, but he cannot say the dates of payments.
Therefore, the Ex.P.13 is not taken into consideration.

Accordingly, it is held that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,670/- towards medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. right distal both bone forearm fracture.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 11 days from 18-03-2022 to 28-03-2022, in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaiedics, Bengaluru.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before the accident he was working in Logistic Company and was earning sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same, he has produced salary certificates (total 3), which are marked as Ex.P.12.
But, he has not examined the author of these documents.
The petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 11 days as in-patient at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaiedics, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.

Therefore,
Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 60 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 11 days as in-patient in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaiedics, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Further, it might have took at least 2 months for complete curing of the injuries suffered by him.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses 30,670-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 11,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 8,800-00 6. Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,86,470/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,86,470/-, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization, from the respondent, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,86,470/- (Rupees one lakh eighty six thousand four hundred and seventy only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

3. What order or Award ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. Further, as per the Motor Vehicles Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence Sudharsan Bengali vs Girish.S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66531843/
4 on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to his sole negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of the accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
The investigation officer has also clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and dashing the same to the bicycle of the petitioner.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 52 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner in his Ex.P.5 first information statement has clearly stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.
He has stated that, as he was taking treatment in the hospital and as he was living alone without any support of family member, he could not decide how to proceed legally and hence there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
Further, it was the duty of the concerned officer of the jurisdictional police to immediately visit the said hospital and record the statement of the victim.
There is no document forthcoming in the present case, with respect to discharge of their duty by the hospital authorities or the concerned officer of the jurisdictional Police Station.
In such circumstances the contention of the respondent that, no such accident as alleged by the petitioner has taken place at the given date, time and place of accident and the petitioner in collusion with the Police has falsely implicated the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 in the said accident and has got created false documents in order to claim compensation, does not hold good and are not sustainable.
Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court is of the opinion that, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate and Ex.P.9 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
As per the said documents, the petitioner has sustained right distal both bone forearm fracture.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that,
the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW-6038 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.decision:
ix) Future medical expenses:
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses 30,670-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 11,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 8,800-00 6. Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil
Total Rs. 1,86,470-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,86,470/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,86,470/-, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization, from the respondent, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,86,470/- (Rupees one lakh eighty six thousand four hundred and seventy only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
